clue.text: What the purchaser of unseasoned timber gets ?

definitions.text: What the purchaser of unseasoned timber gets ?

parts.words: What the purchaser of unseasoned timber gets ?
parts.note: unseasoned wood is raw, and deal is a kind of softwood timber

explanation.surface: A question about what a timber buyer receives when the wood is still green.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the buyer of green softwood gets 'raw' (unseasoned) 'deal' (pine or fir planks); the idiom means unfair treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being treated unfairly or getting a poor bargain.

clue.text: .Take them round the town

parts.note: a road built in a loop around a town lets drivers bypass its centre

explanation.surface: An instruction to escort some visitors on a tour of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take them round' suggests showing guests the sights; it really means driving on roads that circle the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Bypass routes forming a circuit around an urban centre.

clue.text: Resting-places of the brave

parts.note: a brave is an old term for a Native American warrior, whose shelter was a conical tent

explanation.surface: Sounds like a phrase for heroes' graves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resting-places of the brave' suggests war graves; here 'brave' is the noun for a Native American warrior, and his resting-place is his tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dome-shaped huts or tents used by some Native American peoples.

clue.text: New site meant for a restaurant

indicators.note: a new version of these words has their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A building plot earmarked for an eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the nine letters of SITE MEANT. An estaminet is a small French café or bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French café selling food and drink.

clue.text: High speed beat

definitions.meaning: 'at a great ...' means at high speed

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal: a fast pace, and to thrash or defeat.

clue.text: Don't take a dip here if you don't like chaff

definitions.text: Don't take a dip here if you don't like chaff

parts.words: Don't take a dip here if you don't like chaff
parts.note: a lucky-dip barrel at a fete is filled with husks of grain, with prizes buried in them

explanation.surface: A warning to swimmers who dislike being teased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a dip' suggests swimming and 'chaff' suggests teasing; the British fete game has you rummage in a tub of bran for a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A British lucky-dip game: prizes buried in a tub of husks.

clue.text: State of mind in which Chesterton wrote detective stories ?

definitions.text: State of mind in which Chesterton wrote detective stories ?

parts.words: State of mind in which Chesterton wrote detective stories ?
parts.note: G. K. Chesterton's detective was the priest Father Brown, so his casebook could be called a study of that sleuth

explanation.surface: A question about G. K. Chesterton's mood when writing his mysteries.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterton's detective is Father Brown, so his stories are a 'Brown study'; the phrase also means a daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a reverie or absent-minded musing.

clue.text: Cannot a woman act in this capacity ?

definitions.text: Cannot a woman act in this capacity ?

parts.words: Cannot a woman act in this capacity ?
parts.note: split after its first letter the role reads as a man's title, which a woman cannot hold, yet any woman can represent others

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman may take on a certain role.
explanation.walkthrough: Split after its first letter the role sounds like a gentleman, closed to women; it is in fact a representative's job, open to anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who acts on behalf of another, a representative.

clue.text: Easter's tricky puzzles

indicators.note: something tricky is twisted, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters of the word with its S kept

explanation.surface: Seasonal brain-teasers set at Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges EASTERS, keeping the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasers are puzzling problems or riddles.

clue.text: She might take an Italian lady poison

definitions.text: She might take an Italian lady poison

parts.words: She might take an Italian lady poison
parts.note: a girl's name followed by the Italian word for lady, donna, makes the name of deadly nightshade

explanation.surface: A woman poisoning an Italian lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Add DONNA (Italian for 'lady') and this girl's name becomes BELLADONNA, the poison deadly nightshade. 'take' means add, not poison.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, Italian for 'beautiful'.

clue.text: Close on the beginning of tea-time, or sometime later

indicators.note: one piece placed on, that is after, the other

parts.note: near or close means nigh

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something nearly at tea-time, or a bit later.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGH (close) with T, the first letter of 'tea-time', added on. 'or' links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours come later in the day than tea-time.

clue.text: Time, gentlemen, please is not quite fatal

definitions.meaning: the landlord's cry at a British pub's shutting time, the shout that ends the evening's drinking

explanation.definitionFit: A pub's last-orders shout heard at shutting time, and a narrow escape from disaster.

clue.text: Makes Venus ready to embrace Mars ?

definitions.text: Makes Venus ready to embrace Mars ?

parts.words: Makes Venus ready to embrace Mars ?
parts.note: the famous Venus de Milo statue has lost its limbs, so to hug anyone she would need new ones fitted

explanation.surface: A love scene between the gods Venus and Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: The armless Venus de Milo would need her arms restored to embrace anyone; the word normally means equips with weapons again, apt for the war god Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies with weapons again, here read as giving back limbs.

clue.text: Gossip is to them a curse

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk about a person

explanation.surface: Someone who hates gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA (a collection of gossip) + THEM + A; 'is to' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is a formal ecclesiastical malediction, hence something cursed.

clue.text: One law term can produce a fruitful result

indicators.note: the words can be reworked to produce new ones, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A legal term whose outcome is productive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can produce' rearranges ONE LAW TERM. 'fruitful result' plays on 'fruitful' meaning productive.
explanation.definitionFit: A large melon is a fruit, so it is literally a fruity outcome.

clue.text: Page includes this crime at the Framley establishment

indicators.note: the word Page includes this crime to make up the establishment, so taking Page away leaves the crime

parts.note: Trollope's novel Framley Parsonage names a vicar's house at Framley
taken as written

explanation.surface: A page boy embroiled in a crime at a household called Framley.
explanation.walkthrough: The house is from Trollope's novel 'Framley Parsonage'. 'includes' runs backwards here: the page holds the crime to make the house, so taking the page away leaves the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: They don't think for themselves, as a rule

definitions.text: They don't think for themselves, as a rule

parts.words: They don't think for themselves, as a rule
parts.note: people who habitually put others first rarely consider their own interests

explanation.surface: Sounds like a complaint about people who never use their own brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't think for themselves' suggests lack of independent thought; it means they think of others rather than themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfless people who put the welfare of others first.

clue.text: Not low curs, necessarily

parts.note: split in two the word suggests dogs placed underneath, but it means those expected to lose

explanation.surface: A defence of dogs against being called mongrels.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'under dogs' it suggests lowly mongrels; it means outsiders expected to lose, who need not be base at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors or groups thought least likely to win.

clue.text: It's silly to be out of touch, for example

definitions.meaning: touch is one of the five senses, so lacking it is being without a sense

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the word as 'sense-less': touch is an example of a sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish and lacking reason; also, literally, deprived of a faculty such as touch.

clue.text: Diminutive schoolman has a winning margin

parts.note: something diminutive is small or short
the head is the man in charge of a school

explanation.surface: A small headmaster wins a race.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing a short head is the smallest winning distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-racing term for the narrowest victory distance.

clue.text: Constrained to make an old gibe

indicators.note: the letters are used to make a new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone forced to repeat a stale insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges OLD GIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being compelled or bound to do something.

clue.text: He's not a wanderer-on the contrary

indicators.note: the contrary of the word is its letters running the other way

parts.note: a nomad wanders without a fixed home

explanation.surface: A man insisting he is no drifter.
explanation.walkthrough: NOMAD (wanderer) read backwards gives a man's name; 'on the contrary' signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so it can stand for 'he'.

clue.text: I've become attached to a spinster. Make a note of it

indicators.note: one piece is joined onto the end of the other

parts.note: an unmarried woman is addressed as Miss

explanation.surface: A remark about getting engaged to an unmarried woman, then writing it down.
explanation.walkthrough: IVE joined onto MISS (a spinster).
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a letter or written message.

clue.text: It could' be me, in the middle of the game

definitions.text: It could' be me, in the middle of the game

parts.words: It could' be me, in the middle of the game
parts.note: the letters m and e form the latter half of the word time, and the break comes midway through a match

explanation.surface: A player hoping to be involved mid-match.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is half of TIME, so 'half-time' could be 'me'; it is also the interval in the middle of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval at the midpoint of a sports match.

clue.text: Its capital reduction was a Herculean task

definitions.text: Its capital reduction was a Herculean task

parts.words: Its capital reduction was a Herculean task
parts.note: Hercules had to cut off the many heads of a serpent that regrew them, so reducing its heads was his labour

explanation.surface: A finance story about slashing capital being a huge job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital reduction' sounds financial; 'capital' means heads, and cutting off the many-headed serpent's heads was one of Hercules' labours.
explanation.definitionFit: The many-headed water serpent of Greek myth killed by Hercules.

clue.text: Sound evidence: of motoring in Dickens

definitions.meaning: car horns make short blasts, the noise that tells you a car is about
A character in Dickens's Dombey and Son

explanation.definitionFit: Short blasts on a car horn, and the surname of a hapless suitor in Dickens's Dombey and Son.

clue.text: Nothing in the vessel, .but he provisioned himself from it

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a cruse is a small earthenware jar or pot
zero, a ring shape like the letter O

explanation.surface: An empty ship's hold that someone still lived off.
explanation.walkthrough: O inside CRUSE (a small jar). The definition refers to Robinson Crusoe salvaging stores from his wrecked ship; 'vessel' does double duty in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's castaway stocked his island camp with stores from the wreck.

clue.text: This bird doesn't

parts.note: the bird's name is also the verb for boasting, yet this black bird caws rather than doing what a cockerel does

explanation.surface: A three-word puzzle about a bird that doesn't do something.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's name is also the verb for a cockerel's call or for boasting, which this black bird never does: it caws.
explanation.definitionFit: A large black bird of the genus Corvus.

clue.text: It takes the lead

parts.note: a lead is clipped onto the band round a dog's neck; the clerical version marks a church leader

explanation.surface: Someone going first or taking charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the lead' suggests being in front; literally a dog's lead clips to it. It is also a priest's white collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A band round a dog's neck, or a clergyman's stiff white collar.

clue.text: She can exist on nothing but fruit

indicators.note: one piece is set on the other, so they sit side by side

parts.note: zero, shaped like the letter O
to live is to exist

explanation.surface: A woman who survives without eating anything but fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: O (nothing) + LIVE (exist). 'She' also fits, as Olive is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The small oily stone fruit of the Mediterranean tree.

clue.text: Writer gets 50 per cent African capital on completion

indicators.note: half the city's name is kept and the other half dropped

parts.note: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer is paid half his fee in Ethiopia's capital when the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: Addis Ababa is Ethiopia's capital, and its first five letters are exactly half its ten. 'completion' puts the second piece at the end. Joseph Addison was an 18th-century essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison, essayist and co-founder of The Spectator.

clue.text: Theirs the dirty work

parts.note: people or machines that clean clothes deal with soiled items, the grubby job of laundry

explanation.surface: Someone is left with the unpleasant jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dirty work' suggests underhand deeds; literally laundry workers handle dirty clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: People who clean clothes or dishes, laundering things.
